old.name: Acropolis Museum
old.teaser: The top floor is twisted 23 degrees to face the temple 300 metres uphill.
old.text: Bernard Tschumi's 2009 building floats on more than 100 concrete pillars, set so as not to crush the early-Christian streets dug out beneath it — you cross the excavation on glass to get in. The top gallery turns 23 degrees off the building's grid so the frieze hangs in the Parthenon's own orientation, 300 metres away. Between 2011 and 2015 the museum laser-cleaned its five Caryatids in the open hall, not a closed lab; the work took the IIC Keck Award in 2012. The sixth sister's plinth stands pointedly empty, for London.
old.meta: EUR 20 (reduced 10) · Summer (Apr-Oct): Mon 9-17, Tue-Sun 9-20, Fri to 22 · Winter: Mon-Thu 9-17, Fri to 22, Sat-Sun 9-20

old.name: National Archaeological Museum
old.teaser: Room 38 holds the oldest geared machine known — bronze that predicted eclipses.
old.text: Around Easter 1900, sponge divers from Symi sheltering off Antikythera found a Roman-era wreck 50 metres down. The Navy hauled bronzes up through the winter of 1900-01; one corroded lump lay unread until 1902, when it split open and showed gear wheels — the Antikythera mechanism, a 2nd-1st century BC astronomical calculator whose match would not appear for another thousand years. Every surviving fragment sits in Room 38, the unmatched bronze halls around it. Come at the 8:00 opening for the Mycenaean gold, or Tuesday evening once the tour groups have gone.
old.meta: EUR 20 · Summer (4 May-15 Nov 2026): Wed-Mon 8-20, Tue 13-20 · Winter: Wed-Mon 8:30-15:30, Tue 13-20 · free 1st & 3rd Sun Nov-Mar

old.name: Benaki Museum of Greek Culture
old.teaser: One family's mansion tells Greece whole, Bronze Age to 1922.
old.text: In 1930 Antonis Benakis — Alexandrian cotton heir, brother of the novelist Penelope Delta — gave his family's neoclassical house and his life's collecting to the state; the museum opened in 1931 with Benakis as its unpaid director, buying and begging objects for it until he died in 1954. Gilded 18th-century carved-wood reception rooms from Kozani mansions stand reinstalled whole, candle-dark and intact. Thursday's free 18:00-24:00 hours, rooftop café at dusk, are the nearest Athens keeps to a weekly open house.
old.meta: EUR 12 (reduced 6); temporary shows extra · Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat 10-18, Thu 10-24, Sun 10-16, closed Tue

old.name: Museum of Cycladic Art
old.teaser: 5,000-year-old marble figurines that Picasso and Brancusi made modern.
old.text: 19th-century scholars called these folded-arm marble figures 'ugly idols' — then Picasso, Modigliani and Brancusi took their abstraction and made them ancestors of modernism. The Goulandris shipping family collected them from the 1960s and opened the museum in 1986; its annex, Ernst Ziller's 1895 Stathatos Mansion, carries the collection out to Vasilissis Sofias through one of the city's finest neoclassical interiors. The figures sit spotlit in black-walled silence; a Jeff Koons show runs through 2026. The café and shop are ticket-free any day.
old.meta: EUR 12 permanent (reduced 9); EUR 16 combo with show · Mon/Wed/Fri/Sat 10-17, Thu 10-20, Sun 11-17, closed Tue

old.name: Numismatic Museum (Iliou Melathron)
old.teaser: Schliemann's Troy palazzo — you walk on mosaics of his own finds.
old.text: Ernst Ziller's Iliou Melathron — 'the Palace of Troy' — was the most extravagant private house in 1880s Athens: Italian craftsmen laid Pompeiian mosaic floors of Schliemann's finds from Troy and Mycenae, and the excavator dictated Homeric mottoes for the walls. It served fifty years as Greece's Supreme Court, then reopened in 1998 holding some 500,000 coins. The house, not the coins, is the reason to come — and the garden café under Ziller's palms stays open past museum hours (see gem g-schliemann-garden).
old.meta: EUR 10 (reduced 5) · Wed-Mon 08:30-15:30, closed Tue · 'Money and Society' hall closed for maintenance 2026

old.name: Byzantine & Christian Museum
old.teaser: The 1,500 years every visitor skips, in a duchess's 1848 villa.
old.text: The collection lives in Villa Ilissia, the 1848 winter estate Stamatios Kleanthis built on the old Ilissos bank for Sophie de Marbois-Lebrun, Duchess of Plaisance — American-born, Paris-formed, who spent her fortune on Greek schooling and charity and held herself apart from Otto's court. Since 1930 the villa has held over 25,000 icons, mosaics, manuscripts and marbles, among them the mosaic Virgin Episkepsis — thousands of gold tesserae holding the light like candleflame. Come early, then the sunken courtyard gardens before the close.
old.meta: EUR 8 (reduced 4) · Wed-Mon 08:30-15:30, closed Tue (confirm by phone; hours have varied)

old.name: EMST — National Museum of Contemporary Art
old.teaser: The Fix brewery, where the art argues with now, not the past.
old.text: The building is Takis Zenetos's 1957 modernist remodel of the Fix brewery — a postwar industrial landmark half-demolished in the 1990s for the metro, then left derelict for decades before EMST moved in. In 2017 documenta left Kassel for the first time in its history and made this its Athens base under the banner 'Learning from Athens' — the point the city's contemporary scene stopped reading as provincial. Video light spills down raw stairwells across seven floors; Katerina Gregos has directed since 2021.
old.meta: EUR 10 (reduced 5) · Tue-Sun 11-19, Thu 11-22, closed Mon · first Thursday free 18:00-22:00 (not Jul-Aug)

old.name: Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center (SNFCC)
old.teaser: The 600-million-euro gift that handed Athens back its sea horizon.
old.text: It stands on the silted Faliro delta where the city's old racecourse ran down to the water — land last used as Olympic parking in 2004. The Stavros Niarchos Foundation paid the lot, over EUR 600 million, and on 23 February 2017, mid-debt-crisis, simply handed the keys — opera house, national library, 21-hectare park — to the Greek state. Climb the tilted park to the lighthouse reading room and the axis runs straight out over the Salamis strait; below you, the Saronic. Renzo Piano; LEED Platinum, 2016.
old.meta: Free (performances and some events ticketed) · Park and site daily 06:00-24:00 · Library and Greek National Opera per programme

old.name: Melissinos Art — The Poet Sandal Maker
old.teaser: Third-generation sandal-maker who fitted Jackie Onassis and, family telling has it, the Beatles.
old.text: Georgios Melissinos opened beside the Ancient Agora at Pandrossou 89 in 1920; his son Stavros — a published poet, hence the name — turned the ancient sandal into a fashion object in the mid-1950s and fitted Jackie Onassis, Sophia Loren, Maria Callas and Barbra Streisand. Priced out of Pandrossou around the 2004 Olympics, the shop passed to Pantelis, trained at Parsons in New York, and settled at Tziraion 16, 170 m east of the Acropolis Museum. Every pair is hand-fitted, edges burnished, straps trimmed to your foot — not a grab-and-go stop.
old.meta: VISIT Tue–Sat 10:00–18:00 · closed Sun–Mon · call ahead +30 210 3219247 · bespoke, order days early

craft:Tsakirian Lutherie.group: The others, and what each is missing

old.name: Tsakirian Lutherie
old.teaser: The bouzouki bench that armed Chiotis and Kazantzidis — the direct rebetiko thread of this guide.
old.text: Agop Tsakirian, an Armenian refugee from Smyrna, built his first oud in Athens in 1924; his son Onnig opened the Aristotelous Street shop in 1959 and in 1962 cut Manolis Chiotis an all-black bouzouki, and Stelios Kazantzidis played Tsakirian too. Karolos kept his own workshop in Astoria, New York for 17 years before coming home in 1993, and the fourth generation — his daughter Veanous — chose the bench over academia. A striped-bowl bouzouki runs EUR 1,000–3,000 off the rack; a commission takes four to five months. Two artisans at work, not a demo stage.
old.meta: VISIT weekday shop hours · call first +30 210 5240017 · off the rack EUR 1,000–3,000 · commission 4–5 months

craft:Mentis–Antonopoulos Passementerie.group: The others, and what each is missing

old.name: Mentis–Antonopoulos Passementerie (NHMA)
old.teaser: 19th-century Jacquard looms still weaving braid that Dior put on a runway.
old.text: Founded in Nafplio in 1867 and soon moved to Athens to trim the Royal Court and the Palace Guard, the Mentis mill ran a silk workshop, dye house and weaving floor for 144 years. When the firm closed in 2011 the family gave the whole mill and its rare Jacquard looms to the Benaki Museum, which restarted the machines on Polyfimou St in 2012. Maria Grazia Chiuri came here for Greek craft: the twisted cord on the nautical caps of Dior's Cruise 2022 show at the Panathenaic Stadium was made on these benches. Admission is free; braids and tassels sell through the Benaki shop.
old.meta: VISIT Tue–Sat 10:00–15:00 · FREE · closed Sun–Mon and all of August

craft:No class to enrol in.brief: tag 'honestly', NO place/Maps. The honest warning for the craft section: none of the three benches in this guide runs an open class you can enrol in (verify if any does now); what you can do is be fitted or commission. Warn that sandals sold as 'handmade' in the Plaka/Monastiraki tourist strip are not all made on the premises (only if you can source it; otherwise keep it to the enrolment point).

old.name: Athénée (ex-Zonars)
old.teaser: The grand café that outlived its own name — a 1939 mosaic floor recreated tessera by tessera.
old.text: Karolos Zonaras, a chocolate industrialist back from America, opened Zonars in 1939, in the curved Art Deco corner of the Army Share Fund block; Mercouri, Loren, Quinn and Elytis sat under the walnut. K-Studio's 2016 restoration recreated the 1939 marble-mosaic floor tessera by tessera and kept the gilded bar and 1950s red-velvet chairs. In 2019 the room lost its name in court — judges ruled the space, not the word, was the landmark — and became Athénée. A discreet weekday-morning laptop passes; after dark it dresses up, DJ sets until 03:30.
old.meta: ORDER a slow coffee at the gilded bar, or the strawberry pancake stack · HOURS daily 09:00–03:30 · grand-café prices, not budget coffee

old.name: Winter Garden — Hotel Grande Bretagne
old.teaser: Afternoon tea under a stained-glass ceiling — the closest thing Athens keeps to a Viennese café-salon.
old.text: The daylit heart of the 1874 Grande Bretagne: a stained-glass ceiling over walnut and marble, silver-service hush. Theophil Hansen — who later drew the Academy — built it as the Dimitriou mansion in 1842; the cook Efstathios Lampsas borrowed 800,000 drachmas in 1874 to make it a hotel; the building served as Greek, then Nazi, then British headquarters across 1940–44. A discreet laptop passes at a quiet lobby table on a weekday morning; camping through the 15:00–18:00 tea service would be tone-deaf.
old.meta: TEA daily 12:00–20:00, sixteen-blend list, Parliament across Syntagma · smart casual · five-star prices

old.name: Nummus — Numismatic Museum garden café
old.teaser: The calmest garden coffee within 200 metres of Syntagma — and by 15:30 in summer, it is over.
old.text: An 800 m² walled garden behind Schliemann's Iliou Melathron — 'Palace of Ilion' — laid out for the excavator of Troy by royal architect Ernst Ziller around 1880. Century-old trees, plaster copies of ancient gods, and a pomegranate tree (ροδιά) reputedly planted by Schliemann, said to be the only one of its kind in Greece. A hours-trap: in summer it shuts at 15:30 and all day Tuesday — the listings promising evenings to 22:00 describe the winter regime. Outdoor tables, no visible plugs; best 08:30–11:00, before tour-group hour.
old.meta: HOURS summer (1 Apr–31 Oct) Wed–Mon 08:30–15:30, closed Tue; winter daily 08:00–22:00 · bring a battery

old.name: Black Duck Garden — Athens City Museum bistrot
old.teaser: A royal garden hiding sixty metres off Stadiou, where coffee comes with birdsong instead of traffic.
old.text: The garden of the 1833–34 Vouros mansion, requisitioned in 1836 as the first royal residence of King Otto and Queen Amalia while the real palace — today's Parliament — went up. Amalia, who laid out the capital's first public gardens, planted here herself; the bistrot pours coffee under a palm the museum attributes to her hand. Opened in 2008 as the first Greek museum bistrot, it keeps one of the centre's last quiet gardens. Fine for a quiet weekday morning hour, no visible plugs — not a full workday.
old.meta: HOURS garden through 15 Oct, 09:00 till late; patio year-round · museum closed Tuesdays

old.name: National Library reading rooms
old.teaser: The honest best free desk in Attica — plugs, Wi-Fi, enforced silence.
old.text: Renzo Piano tilted the 2016 SNFCC park into an artificial hill so the National Library reading rooms could sit beneath it — free, no card, open daily 09:00–24:00, with power outlets, Wi-Fi and enforced silence, 4.5 km from Syntagma. No calls or meetings inside. Delta, upstairs in the same Renzo Piano building, took two MICHELIN stars and a Green Star in the 2022 guide, at its very first evaluation.
old.meta: HOURS Open Reading Rooms daily 09:00–24:00 · Free · Syngrou 364, Kallithea (4.5 km from Syntagma)

old.name: Okupa
old.teaser: Work by day, stay for the record — hostel, desks and a listening bar in one address.
old.text: Opened 2024 on a quiet Kerameikos street, Okupa folds a hostel, a co-working room, a kitchen and a listening bar into one address — laptops fill the day tables from breakfast at 07:30, then a vinyl booth takes over Tuesday to Sunday, with live jazz in the courtyard on Sundays. The one room in Athens where you can work, eat muhammara toast with smoked mackerel, and stay for the record without leaving the building.
old.meta: HOURS from 07:30 (breakfast) · listening sessions Tue–Sun, live jazz Sun · Psaromiligkou 9, Kerameikos

old.name: Kick
old.teaser: Part cafe, part workspace, part exhibition room — built to be sat in.
old.text: A Kypseli side street off Plateia Amerikis holds Kick — part cafe, part workspace, part exhibition room, open Mon–Fri from 07:30, pouring Mr Bean single-origin espresso with pastries from its sister microbakery Flake across the road. LiFO's line on it — the hub that makes you feel 'we became Europe' — is really a verdict on new Kypseli itself. More neighbourhood hub than hush, so good for working with a coffee, less for silence or speed.
old.meta: HOURS Mon–Fri 07:30–19:00, Sat–Sun 09:00–19:00 · EUR 3–8 · Sporadon 26, Kypseli

old.name: Dexameni
old.teaser: Kolonaki's last great literary square-kafeneio — order ouzo and the plane-tree table is yours all evening.
old.text: An open-air plane-tree square above Kolonaki, named for Hadrian's 2nd-century reservoir still behind the railings, beside the Cine Dexameni open-air cinema, Elytis's statue on the flagstones. A century ago its kafeneio was the open-air salon of Greek letters — Varnalis, Kazantzakis, the '30s-generation poets. Its immortal moment came one 1906 morning, when Pavlos Nirvanas ambushed Alexandros Papadiamantis, who had refused every camera, and took the only classic portrait of him right here. No laptops, by culture rather than any ban — bring a book, not a screen.
old.meta: HOURS daily 10:00–02:00 · about €25–30 a head · reopened around 2012, unchanged; the room is the open square, so weather decides

old.name: Taf Coffee
old.teaser: The 2009 bar that lit Athens' third wave — cup-first, not a workday.
old.text: Yiannis Taloumis turned his family's 1990s Greek-coffee firm into a specialty house and opened this Benaki bar in 2009 — widely credited as the ignition of Athens' third wave. 2014 was the annus mirabilis: a world Brewers Cup title for Stefanos Domatiotis, a podium for Chris Loukakis at the Barista Championship, an SCAE Lifetime Achievement award for Taloumis — one storefront, three world laurels in a year. The quieter first-floor room takes a weekday-morning laptop; come for the cup, not the plate.
old.meta: HOURS daily, morning into early evening · EUR 3–7 · Emmanouil Benaki 7
